title: Week 0 · Day 1 · The briefing
bodyHtml:
Week 0 · Day 1 · 100 minutes. Save a prediction, test it, keep a timeline, then begin the four-phase mission.

Learning targets

  • Predict before testing and name evidence that could challenge the claim.
  • Record what was planned, what happened and why the explanation changed.

Before class

Two equal paper sheets per group, one left flat and one crumpled; a clear floor and a consistent low release height. Each learner saves their own prediction before the drop. Keep the first response; the later record captures revision.

Lesson flow

TimeAction and evidence
0–10Show the two paper shapes. Each learner predicts the landing order and explains why. Save the prediction before the demo.
10–25Test from the same height, repeat once. Record the planned setup, actual observation and evidence source.
25–40Partners compare the observation with their first prediction. Each learner sketches the setup and records what changed and why.
40–65Read the fictional mission briefing. Notice/wonder and question sorting are optional discussion practice, not additional required submissions.
65–80Connect the actual four phases: Track it (motion, forces, structures); Move it (energy); Sense it (fluids, waves, electromagnetism); Power it, prove it (generation and capstone).
80–95Individual exit: use test evidence to support or challenge the prediction and propose a second test. Name evidence that could prove the revised claim wrong.
95–100Self-rate 1–3 using the saved evidence. Preview the same routine with the motion detector next class.

Teaching decision

If the learner copied an outcome without comparing it with the prediction, ask for the missing evidence link. If the timeline lacks a controlled setup, repeat the test with explicit height and release conditions. Language support carries the same reasoning demand.

Current lesson evidence and projection

Use the class session’s linked target and exit screens. The current learner task and the projector read the same blocks; self-rating uses 1–3 after the individual exit.

  • diagnostic · briefing-prediction-20260913: Before testing: predict the landing order of the flat and crumpled sheets dropped from the same height. Explain your reason and name an observation that would challenge your prediction. Save now; record revisions separately after the test.
  • main · briefing-test-record-20260913: Keep your first prediction. Sketch the two paper shapes and record the test timeline below: planned setup, actual observation, and an evidence-based revision. Use your classroom result. If working independently, perform the same low-height paper drop over a clear floor; repeat it once.
  • exit · briefing-evidence-exit-20260913: Use one observation from your paper-drop test to support or challenge your initial prediction. Explain what you would change or keep in a second test, and name evidence that could prove your revised claim wrong.

Check the reasoning and evidence, not completion alone. Optional practice remains available on the learner’s device and in the projector block picker. Preserve the first saved prediction; revisions belong in the later evidence task.

title: Week 0 · Day 2 · The detector · first touch
bodyHtml:
Week 0 · Day 2 · 100 minutes. Hands → record → partner talk → individual explanation.

Learning targets

  • I can write a prediction and lock it before I test, and say what evidence would prove me wrong. / Puedo escribir una predicción y fijarla antes de probar, y decir qué evidencia demostraría que estoy equivocado.

Lesson flow

TimeTeacher and student actions
0–15 minPredict the trace

Introduce detector boundaries and safe walking space. Ask for a predicted line before revealing the live trace.

15–50 minWalk and observe

Take turns moving toward, away from, and standing still in front of the detector. Keep the starting position and direction explicit.

50–70 minRecord the trace

Use the lesson sketch to show one observed trace with labels.

70–90 minPartner explanation

Explain which line segment means moving and which means stopped. Use the bilingual sentence frame.

90–100 minIndividual exit

Cite features of the saved trace and lock a prediction for another walk.

Saved evidence

  • RECORD · Sketch what the screen showed for YOUR walk. Label where you walked toward, away, and stopped — in either language. · REGISTRA · Dibuja lo que mostró la pantalla en TU caminata. Marca dónde caminaste hacia, lejos y parado — en cualquier idioma.
  • When I walked ___, the line went ___. When I stopped, the line was ___.
  • w00d2-rate
  • Use your detector trace from today. Describe one part where you walked and one part where you stopped. Cite a feature of the line for each, and state one prediction you would lock before a second walk.

Next teaching decision

Use the main artifact and individual exit to decide whether the learner needs a model, a measurement check, or a second attempt. Do not score a prediction for merely matching the outcome; inspect its reasoning and revision from evidence. Keep language support separate from physics mastery.

title: Week 0 · Day 3 · Teams, roles, the timeline
bodyHtml:
Week 0 · Day 3 · 100 minutes. Hands → record → partner talk → individual explanation.

Learning targets

  • I can keep an engineering timeline: what I planned, what actually happened, and why they differ. / Puedo llevar una línea de tiempo de ingeniería: lo que planeé, lo que pasó realmente y por qué son diferentes.

Lesson flow

TimeTeacher and student actions
0–15 minAssign roles

Establish who handles materials, records the timeline, and checks evidence; rotate roles during later builds.

15–35 minRead the packet

Locate the planning, actual-events, and reasoning parts of the timeline. Model an entry using an ordinary classroom event.

35–65 minWrite entry one

Record what the team planned and what actually happened, using a specific sequence of events.

65–85 minPartner check

Ask a partner to distinguish the planned event from the observed result. Revise ambiguity.

85–100 minIndividual exit

Use timeline entry one to name a change for next time and the evidence behind it.

Saved evidence

  • w00d3-timeline
  • w00d3-rate
  • Use timeline entry #1. State what your team planned, what actually happened, and one change you will make next time because of that evidence.

Next teaching decision

Use the main artifact and individual exit to decide whether the learner needs a model, a measurement check, or a second attempt. Do not score a prediction for merely matching the outcome; inspect its reasoning and revision from evidence. Keep language support separate from physics mastery.

title: Week 0 · Day 4 · Paper tower · predict before you test
bodyHtml:
Week 0 · Day 4 · 100 minutes. Hands → record → partner talk → individual explanation.

Learning targets

  • I can write a prediction and lock it before I test, and say what evidence would prove me wrong. / Puedo escribir una predicción y fijarla antes de probar, y decir qué evidencia demostraría que estoy equivocado.
  • I can keep an engineering timeline: what I planned, what actually happened, and why they differ. / Puedo llevar una línea de tiempo de ingeniería: lo que planeé, lo que pasó realmente y por qué son diferentes.

Lesson flow

TimeTeacher and student actions
0–10 minLock a height prediction

State a predicted tower height and a reason before handling build materials.

10–30 minBuild the paper tower

Use the authored 20-minute mini-build constraint. Keep the same success measure across groups.

30–55 minMeasure and record

Measure the tower and enter the predicted and actual values with units.

55–75 minExplain the gap

Partners compare prediction and result, then complete the sentence frame.

75–90 minTimeline

Record the planned build, what happened, and the explanation for a change.

90–100 minIndividual exit

Name what will change on the next build and the prediction that will be locked first.

Saved evidence

  • I predict our tower will be ___ cm tall, because ___. Evidence that would prove me wrong: ___.
  • w00d4-data
  • We predicted ___ cm. Our tower was ___ cm. The gap is because ___.
  • w00d4-timeline
  • EXIT · Week 0 · What will you do differently on the next build — and what prediction will you lock first?
  • w00d4-rate

Next teaching decision

Use the main artifact and individual exit to decide whether the learner needs a model, a measurement check, or a second attempt. Do not score a prediction for merely matching the outcome; inspect its reasoning and revision from evidence. Keep language support separate from physics mastery.
